propositions: No headroom guard exists on plan_review/workflow_ops.py (794 LOC) and llm/config.py (793 LOC), both of which exceed the 700-line policy threshold and lack structural defence against module regrowth

A missed registration import (prerequisite_workflow_ops at workflow_ops.py:45) cannot be caught by existing layers—schema treats step names as free-form strings, linter skips unknown steps by design, and test_contracts.py only checks what IS registered—making runtime discovery the only safety net

test_gate_dispatch_seam.py asserts headroom on gate_dispatch.py while describing finalize_verdict call sites that moved to plan_review_recovery.py and workflow_ops.py, making the assertion's justification stale

STEP_REGISTRY is a process-global dict populated by import side effects, and in-process test assertions are masked when other test modules import the same workflow.steps module before the guard runs, making import-caching-dependent tests order-dependent and unreliable

gate-YAML resolution (gates/plan-review.yaml:136 references plan_review_prerequisite_verify_inputs) depends on whether the registration import survives, but no assertion validates that every uses: entry in the gate file resolves in STEP_REGISTRY

Subprocess isolation is required to detect registration failures, because a subprocess with clean sys.modules observes first-import registry population and cannot be masked by test ordering or concurrent test module imports
